message.content:
The scent of cinnamon and damp earth clung to the air, a peculiar perfume for a Saturday morning. Max tugged his beanie lower, shielding his eyes from the weak sunlight struggling through the overcast sky. He’d been awake since 6:00 am, wrestling with folding tables and a temperamental pop-up banner, all for the sake of his friend, Elias. Elias, who had apparently decided, on a whim, to become a purveyor of artisanal bird feeders.

“Are you sure about this?” Max had asked last night, skepticism dripping from his voice. Elias, usually so grounded, so pragmatic, had just shrugged, a mischievous glint in his eyes. “Just want to try something new, Max. Something…tangible.” Tangible, apparently, involved meticulously hand-crafting wooden houses for wrens and finches. Max still didn’t understand it, but he understood Elias, and he knew that arguing was futile. Besides, a weekend out of the city, surrounded by the bustle of the local farmer’s market, wasn’t exactly a hardship.

The stall itself, christened "Feathered Friends & Co.," looked deceptively charming. Elias had a knack for aesthetics, even when the subject matter was decidedly avian. The bird feeders, painted in muted blues and greens with tiny, whimsical details, were displayed on reclaimed wood shelves. A small chalkboard sign, painstakingly lettered by Elias himself, proclaimed the benefits of providing “a safe and stylish haven for your backyard birds.” Max, meanwhile, was responsible for the less glamorous tasks: securing the table legs, ensuring the banner didn't collapse in a gust of wind, and generally preventing Elias from getting distracted by the sheer novelty of it all.

“Right, think we’re ready,” Elias declared, stepping back to survey their handiwork. He smoothed down his hair, a nervous habit Max had come to know well. He was dressed in a simple, worn denim jacket and a faded grey t-shirt, a far cry from the tailored suits he usually favored. It suited him, oddly. He looked…relaxed. Almost unrecognizably so.

A few early shoppers were already milling about, their baskets overflowing with fresh produce and artisanal bread. Max scanned the crowd, half-expecting a familiar face to appear and offer a mocking comment about Elias’s sudden career change. But so far, it was just families and elderly couples, all seemingly absorbed in their weekend rituals.

“Okay, operation ‘attract the feathered clientele’ is officially underway,” Max announced, attempting a lighthearted tone to mask his underlying apprehension. He wasn't entirely sure what Elias was up to, but he was committed to supporting him. Besides, he was genuinely curious to see how this whole thing would play out.

Elias grinned, a genuine, unforced smile that reached his eyes. “Let’s just hope the birds agree.” He picked up a small, robin-sized feeder, turning it over in his hands. “These little guys deserve a good home, don’t you think?”
